items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (durabilityTracker, resolvedLocked, notifyLocked, batchDurableState), exported APIs have docs, and comments explain non-obvious points such as sticky errors and why waitJob never blocks. The one oddity, `b := &batch.durable` in applyInternal, is minor.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go (469 lines) is a clean dedicated type with short functions. But it detects a configured listener with a reflect pointer hack (`reflect.ValueOf(l.BatchDurable).Pointer() != ...noopBatchDurable`). It fires from applyInternal and Batch.SyncWait, not commit.go, and sets walStart in two places.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Retention and subscription limits are named constants, waits use channels with no polling, and close and errors take precedence correctly. Gaps: WaitForJobDurabilityContext ignores ctx. A NoSyncWait batch whose SyncWait is never called never records durability and keeps a reference to the DB in pendingDB.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API is additive and non-sync commits are unchanged. Every Sync commit now takes the global tracker mutex in record() and makes extra NowMono calls even when BatchDurable is unset. The NoSyncWait path changes too: SyncWait now calls d.onBatchDurable.
